item.title: Luka Doncic and the Lakers did some team building at Slovenian nightclub where a Playboy model was hanging out
item.description: Luka Doncic and his Lakers teammates hit a Ljubljana nightclub for team building, but a former Playboy model's reported presence stole headlines.
item.content:encoded:
Can't Luka Doncic and his Los Angeles Lakers teammates do some team building at a Slovenian nightclub in peace? Can't a former Playboy model also happen to be hanging out there?

The answer to that, apparently, is no. The Lakers trip over the weekend to a Ljubljana restaurant, which reportedly also serves as a nightclub, made news in the Slovenian outlet Nedeljski dnevnik.

The exclusive party had strict rules, according to the outlet. There were no pictures or videos allowed inside the nightclub and phones had stickers placed over the cameras.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON’T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Slovenian model Anja Jenko, who appeared on the cover of Playboy back in 2014, was also reported, among others, to have been at the nightclub at the time.

Her attendance became the focus of other headlines, although there were no reports of the model hanging out with any of the players.

ADULT ACTRESS MADISON IVY CRASHED A LAKERS PRIVATE DINNER 'THIS MIGHT BE THE GREATEST MOMENT OF MY WHOLE LIFE'

As was already mentioned, this was a team-building event for the Lakers. A business trip, if you will. The Slovenian media even pointed out "the basketball players are said to mostly hang out with each other."

So what are we doing here? Luka is noticeably thinner. He's been dealing with baby momma drama. There's no LeBron James on the Lakers roster, and he can't team build with the guys in his home country?

This was supposed to be an exclusive party, stickers on camera for a reason. So a former Playboy model was reported to be in the building. What does this have to do with the Los Angeles Lakers and their superstar?

I can't be the only one who doesn’t see a connection here. When did team building at a nightclub become something more just because a former Playboy model was at the same nightclub at the same time?

item.title: California pastor charged with yearslong child molestation as investigators seek more victims: DA
item.description: David Johnson, an Ojai pastor and massage therapist, faces six felony child molestation charges in Ventura County as investigators seek more victims.
item.content:encoded:
A California pastor and massage therapist has pleaded not guilty to charges accusing him of molesting two children under the age of 14 over several years, prosecutors said.

David Johnson, 58, of Ojai, faces six felony child molestation charges in Ventura County, according to the Ventura County District Attorney’s Office.

Investigators are also looking for possible additional victims and have publicly asked anyone with information about Johnson or other possible unreported crimes to come forward.

Johnson is accused of molesting two children who were under 14 years old at the time of the alleged abuse.

Prosecutors said the alleged abuse occurred over several years at locations in Ojai and Oxnard.

SAN FRANCISCO ARCHDIOCESE AGREES TO $395M SETTLEMENT WITH 530 CLERGY ABUSE SURVIVORS

Johnson, who worked as both a pastor and massage therapist, had access to the children through a familial relationship, according to prosecutors.

Authorities have not publicly identified the children.

Johnson faces four felony counts of committing a lewd act upon a child and two felony counts of continuous sexual abuse.

Prosecutors have also filed special allegations involving substantial sexual conduct and the victims being under 14 years old, according to the district attorney’s office.

EX-TEXAS MIDDLE SCHOOL TEACHER SENTENCED TO 33 YEARS FOR SEXUALLY ABUSING 13-YEAR-OLD STUDENT

Johnson was arrested Monday on charges of child molestation by the Ventura County Sheriff’s Office, according to sheriff’s inmate records.

The records show Johnson was arrested shortly before 3 p.m. and booked into the Ventura County Main Jail later that evening.

Johnson appeared in Ventura County Superior Court for his arraignment and pleaded not guilty to all six charges.

He remains in custody without bail and is scheduled to return to Ventura County Superior Court on Friday for a bail review hearing.

HIGH SCHOOL TEACHER WHO ALLEGEDLY HAD SEX WITH STUDENT IN CLOSET NOW FACES CHARGES INVOLVING MORE TEENS

Deputy District Attorney Cesar Ponce of the Ventura County District Attorney’s Office Sexual Assault Unit is prosecuting the case.

Investigators have not said publicly how many additional victims they believe there could be.

The district attorney’s office is asking anyone with information about the case or other possible unreported crimes involving Johnson to contact Ventura County Sheriff’s Office Detective Michael Loth at 805-384-4745.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Ventura County District Attorney’s Office for additional information.

item.title: Jerry Jones has no 'succession plan' for Cowboys leadership: 'Just won't be here to toss my two cents in'
item.description: Jerry Jones said he has no succession plan for the Dallas Cowboys, hinting he will stay involved until he's gone. Troy Aikman weighs in on the future.
item.content:encoded:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones is 83 years old and continues to lead the way in the front office of his organization.

But Jones’ age also poses questions about when he will step aside and have a successor take his place at the head of the Cowboys’ table. Stephen Jones, his son who has been heavily involved in the Cowboys’ decision-making for years, seems to be the easy guess for who will take Jerry’s spot one day.

However, if you ask him about his eventual handing of the torch, Jones scoffs at it.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"I don’t have a succession plan, I don’t. One day, I just won’t be here to toss my two cents in," he told The Athletic.

A comment like that seems to indicate that, until his final breath, Jones will be working to get the Cowboys more Super Bowl rings.

The oil and gas businessman purchased the team for $140 million in February 1989, and the team’s success quickly came thereafter.

JERRY JONES 'OPEN' TO CO-OWNING COWBOYS WITH MARK CUBAN: 'ALL THE RESPECT IN THE WORLD FOR HIM'

The Cowboys won the Super Bowl in 1993, 1994 and 1996, restoring the team’s previous glory after Dallas won Super Bowl VI (1972) and Super Bowl XII (1978) prior to Jones’ ownership.

But the Cowboys have not made it back to the Super Bowl since that 1996 win, and the supporters of "America’s Team" are desperate to see it happen. Each season, it feels the Cowboys have the chance to do so, but they’ve either fallen short in the playoffs, or worse, missed the postseason entirely.

However, the Cowboys remain one of the most valued teams in all of American sports since Jones purchased the club. According to Sportico, the team is valued at an estimated $15.5 billion if he were to sell it today.

Still, fans have been worried over the years whether Jones’ involvement in team affairs has cost them the opportunity to win more rings. And Jones hasn’t been afraid to retort when that notion is brought up by fans and reporters alike.

"I’m not pushing Jerry out by any means, but when that day comes, it’s gonna feel a lot different," Cowboys legendary Hall of Fame quarterback Troy Aikman told The Athletic.

Aikman added that he doesn’t feel Stephen has the same ego that his father has, believing that will "serve" him "well."

Jerry has even said Stephen has been a great right-hand man over the years because he’s kept him in check.

"He’s about as good as anybody I’ve ever been around in giving deference when he should," Jerry explained about his son. "Now, don’t confuse that with lack of intensity. He’ll bite back real hard when he has to. Real hard. He just does it with more grace than I do."

The day will eventually come where Jerry won’t be leading the Cowboys, but it doesn’t sound like it will be anytime soon.

item.title: Former Gitmo prosecutor likens 9/11 trial delay to 'Frankenstein's zombie court'
item.description: Khalid Sheikh Mohammed and three alleged 9/11 co-conspirators will face trial in June 2028 as the Guantánamo military commission sets new deadlines.
item.content:encoded:
Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, the accused mastermind of the Sept. 11 terror attacks, and three alleged co-conspirators will finally stand trial in 2028, as the case against them has languished amid lengthy delays and a protracted process that one expert has likened to "Frankenstein's zombie court."

A military judge on Wednesday set the long-delayed trial for June 5, 2028, while establishing deadlines for the case. Much to the frustration of the loved ones of those who died during the attacks, Mohammed and his alleged co-conspirators have been held at a military detention center in Guantánamo Bay, Cuba, for more than two decades.

The problem, according to Michael Lebowitz, a former Guantánamo military commissions prosecutor, isn't the evidence against the terror suspects — it's the system.

NEW EVIDENCE IN LOCKERBIE PAN AM FLIGHT 103 BOMBING CASE PUSHES FEDERAL JUDGE TO POSTPONE TRIAL

"It's the system and how it evolved and was created. And it's also an issue of Guantánamo Bay itself, where Gitmo is an adequate, albeit expensive, option for things like detaining suspected war criminals and even migrants," Lebowitz told Fox News Digital.

"The problem is that we used to call it the traveling circus because, in order to even conduct the smallest court hearing, everybody has to go to Washington, D.C., and get on an airplane," he continued. "I'm talking judges. I'm talking prosecutors, defense counsel, witnesses and court people."

TRUMP TURNS TO 'ZOMBIE' COURT AFTER BOASBERG POINTED TO IT IN DEPORTATION FIGHT

The case of Mohammed, as well as Walid bin Attash, Mustafa al-Hawsawi and Ammar al-Baluchi, has been delayed for decades amid lengthy legal wrangling, including failed efforts to resolve the case through plea agreements.

The 2028 date sets a timetable for a case that has remained in pretrial proceedings for years as the military commission has addressed disputes over evidence and other legal issues before a trial on the merits can begin, Fox News Digital previously reported.

NEW 9/11 MUSEUM EXHIBIT AIMS TO CONNECT YOUNGER AMERICANS TO THE ATTACKS THROUGH POWERFUL ARTIFACTS

Mohammed, a Pakistani citizen, is accused of masterminding the attacks in which hijackers crashed commercial airliners into the World Trade Center in New York City and the Pentagon. A fourth hijacked plane, United Airlines Flight 93, crashed in Pennsylvania after passengers attempted to overtake the hijackers.

The case has had more than 10 judges, Lebowitz said, meaning lawyers have had to keep relitigating the same "mundane" issues. Lebowitz, an Army veteran, participated in a number of cases in Guantanamo, including the 9/11 case and the bombing of the USS Cole.

TRUMP ADMIN INVOKES 30-YEAR DORMANT TERROR COURT AS IT SEEKS TO DEPORT AFGHAN WOMAN TIED TO ELECTION DAY PLOT

"What I found was that the way the system has kind of been set up and how it evolved and turned into, it's essentially a candy store for defense lawyers, where the judges don't have teeth to control the courtroom like you would in federal court," he said. "It just goes from there where defense lawyers can really grease up the system and grease up the gears and really grind it to a halt."

One issue prosecutors will have to iron out is whether to seek the death penalty, Lebowitz said. Even if Mohammed and the other suspected terrorists are condemned to death, it's highly unlikely to be upheld, he said.

I LOST MY WIFE ON 9/11. PLEASE LET THIS 25TH ANNIVERSARY BELONG TO THE FAMILIES

"You're dealing with cases where, essentially, the defense lawyers would put the CIA on trial for their treatment of detainees after 9/11," he noted.

In 2024, Mohammed, bin Attash and al-Hawsawi agreed to admit their roles in the terror attacks in exchange for serving life sentences and avoiding the death penalty. While some 9/11 families supported the idea, others blasted the deal.

Amid the criticism, the Biden administration withdrew the plea deal, resulting in more litigation.

Fox News Digital's Brittany Miller contributed to this report.

item.title: WATCH: Man accused of aiming flamethrower at officers serving eviction notice in wild bodycam video
item.description: Body-camera video captures the moment Darron Dunn allegedly blasted deputies with a makeshift flamethrower during an Oklahoma City eviction.
item.content:encoded:
A routine eviction call turned into a fiery standoff when an Oklahoma man allegedly blasted deputies with a makeshift flamethrower while a wired car-battery device sat inside his apartment, body-camera video shows.

Body-camera video released by the Oklahoma County Sheriff’s Office captures deputies forcing their way into the dark, cluttered Oklahoma City apartment on Aug. 11 after the tenant, identified as Darron Dunn, 61, allegedly barricaded the entrance.

Deputies had arrived to serve an eviction order shortly before noon. Housing Authority staff unlocked the door, but it would not open all the way. Officers said they found cables connected to the door and an electric wheelchair positioned behind it.

NYC LANDLORD PLEADS FOR HELP AS '9-YEAR-SQUATTER' CONTINUES TO DRAIN HIM DRY IN COURT SAGA: 'TWILIGHT ZONE'

Once inside, a deputy spotted Dunn sitting in a bedroom. The incident report notes Dunn immediately sprayed an aerosol can toward the deputy and a Housing Authority security officer, then allegedly lit it on fire.

The bodycam video showed a bright orange flash as the burst of fire filled the doorway.

"Back up!" an officer can be heard yelling as deputies retreated.

LIVE EXPLOSIVE DEVICE FOUND NEAR HOMELAND SECURITY OFFICE IN CLEVELAND, FORCING MASS EVACUATIONS

Authorities said the deputy felt the "extreme heat" from the flames. The sheriff’s office said the fire traveled about 15 feet in the deputy’s direction.

But the flames were only the start.

As deputies backed out, officers spotted a car battery with wires attached near Dunn, and another wired device near the front door. The video captured the growing alarm inside the apartment.

WATCH: EVICTION STANDOFF TURNS TO WAR ZONE AS GUNMAN KILLS DEPUTY IN AMBUSH, GETS RUN OVER BY ARMORED VEHICLE

"He’s got it hooked up to the battery!" one officer shouted.

"Everybody out! Improvised device! Get out!" another could be heard yelling.

NORTH CAROLINA MAN ARMED WITH FLAMETHROWERS, CROSSBOWS, 500 ROUNDS ARRESTED OUTSIDE CHURCH: POLICE

According to the incident report, the device consisted of rows of butane lighter-fluid and carburetor-cleaner aerosol cans taped together with bare wires attached. 

Deputies evacuated residents from the third floor and nearby levels while the sheriff’s tactical team and bomb squad responded.

Officers later disabled the wires connected to the cans and safely removed Dunn from the apartment in his wheelchair, authorities said.

NYPD OFFICER SHOT, GUNMAN KILLED AFTER ARMED BARRICADED STANDOFF IN BROOKLYN: POLICE

A spokesperson for the Oklahoma County Sheriff’s Office told Fox News Digital that bomb technicians determined the wired aerosol-can device was unlikely to explode as configured. The spokesperson said it could have sparked or heated up if the bare wires touched the car-battery terminal, but technicians did not believe it would detonate.

Dunn was taken to a VA hospital because of medical issues and stress before being placed in a mental hospital, according to the incident report.

Out-of-custody charges were filed against Dunn for assault and battery with a dangerous weapon; possessing, using, manufacturing or threatening to use an incendiary device or explosives; and obstructing an officer.

The sheriff’s office spokesperson said evictions can be "so emotionally charged" and deputies sadly see volatile reactions during such calls. The spokesperson said the confrontation came four years after officers were attacked in another similar eviction-related incident.

In a separate eviction call about a year ago, the spokesperson said, a man allegedly tried to set a deputy on fire before setting himself ablaze and dying.

item.title: Stockard Channing hits first red carpet in 2 years after saying she's a 'recluse'
item.description: Stockard Channing, 82, stepped out at the "Practical Magic 2" London premiere after years of reclusive life in the U.K. after her partner's death.
item.content:encoded:
"Practical Magic" star Stockard Channing made her red carpet return for the first time in two years after settling into a reclusive life in the United Kingdom.

Channing, 82, basked in the flashing lights while attending the European premiere of "Practical Magic 2" at the Odeon Luxe Leicester Square in London Aug. 26.

Earlier this year, Channing confessed she's "happy being a recluse" as she reflected on her quiet lifestyle after leaving the United States following the death of her longtime partner.

‘GREASE’ STAR STOCKARD CHANNING SAYS SHE’S ‘HAPPY BEING A RECLUSE’ AFTER LEAVING AMERICA

The actress, who reprised her role as Aunt Franny in the highly anticipated sequel, sported a chic blue suit with a white button-down and chain-link jewelry to mark her red carpet return.

The following day, Channing turned heads in a monochrome emerald green ensemble for a London photo call. The "Practical Magic" sequel brings stars Nicole Kidman, Sandra Bullock and Dianne Wiest back together 28 years after the original film's release.

Channing began living in London "just before COVID," a move she envisioned after the 2014 death of her partner of 25 years, producer Daniel Gillham.

"I've lived alone since I lost Daniel and I'm happy being a recluse," Channing wrote in an essay for The Sunday Times. "I was married four times before Daniel, and they all represent epochs of me."

She admitted that Gilham's death "was more devastating than I realized; it had a lag effect."

"The pattern of my life shifted, so I shifted my life from Maine," she wrote of the move, which also vaguely coincided with Trump's second presidential bid.

Her days of stardom are slightly different from now. The "Six Degrees of Separation" actress detailed her morning routine, which begins at 7 a.m. when her dog wakes her up.

By 10 a.m., Channing pursues a "bit of exercise" but admitted that her "favorite exercise days are when I play hooky."

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"I know that exercising is the right thing to do but my brain tells me to go hide behind the bike sheds," she wrote. "Lunch is my first meal of the day and I can follow a recipe, but if my ramen doesn't work out I give it to the dog.

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

"If I'm leaving the apartment I comb my hair, but I don't have a wardrobe of designer outfits. Well, I do, but they're all from the Eighties and Nineties. Do I care how I look? Most actors do although part of your job is not being self-conscious.

"But I've never considered myself as beautiful. And I'm not a celebrity 'tart.' I'm just me, take it or leave it."

item.title: Mamdani stands by DSA insider accused of stiffing landlord amid $1.4M townhome makeover
item.description: Mayor Zohran Mamdani twice declined to distance himself from NYC-DSA co-chair Gustavo Gordillo, who faces a pending rent case and scrutiny over his union credentials and family townhouse renovation.
item.content:encoded:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani repeatedly declined to distance himself from embattled New York City Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) co-chair Gustavo Gordillo, after being pressed on allegations that the DSA leader failed to pay thousands in rent on a Crown Heights apartment while his family spent a reported $1.4 million renovating the NYC townhouse where he lives—a contrast critics say is difficult to square with the anti-landlord, rent-abolitionist socialist housing agenda he helps champion.

Mamdani said Sunday that people working for a "more affordable life" and a "fairer life" for New Yorkers "should be welcomed into this work." When asked again Monday whether Gordillo should step down and whether he condemned allegations that Gordillo lied about his employment, the mayor said he welcomed anyone committed to making New York "a city that everyone can belong to." Meanwhile, asked directly whether he condemned Gordillo’s alleged actions and lying, Mamdani ended the exchange: "Thank you very much."

Gordillo, an Ivy League graduate who as a NYC-DSA co-chair met weekly with Mamdani and his campaign manager as the group coordinated fundraising, field and communications efforts, later served on Mamdani’s Economic Development & Workforce Development transition committee, according to public reporting. 

He is named in a pending Brooklyn Housing Court case, in which a former landlord alleges Gordillo failed to pay $5,000 in rent on a $2,500-a-month Crown Heights apartment, while his family's townhouse was undergoing its $1.4 million in renovations, according to the New York Post. Gordillo's family reportedly bought the Bed-Stuy townhouse in 2019 for $935,000, while Gordillo’s father has said it is for Gordillo and his brother to live in.

SOCIALIST BIGWIG BLASTS THE WEALTHY WHILE LIVING IN $1.4M BROOKLYN BROWNSTONE WITH EYEBROW-RAISING BACKSTORY

"The Democratic Socialists of America have become the Double Standards of America — demanding transparency, fairness, and accountability from everyone else while ignoring serious questions about one of their own," Rev. Kevin McCall, a Brooklyn pastor who also assists tenants in New York City Housing Authority complexes, told the New York Post.

"The allegations surrounding NYC chapter co-chair Gustavo Gordillo raise troubling questions about whether he misled working-class New Yorkers about where he lived, how he obtained housing, and his labor credentials. DSA leaders and elected officials must answer these questions publicly and call for Gordillo’s resignation," the Reverend added.

NEW YORK CITY MAYOR ZOHRAN MAMDANI STRUGGLES TO DEFINE 'WORKING CLASS'

Neither Mamdani's office, the NYC-DSA nor Gordillo, responded to Fox News Digital's requests for comment. The housing case involving Gordillo remains pending and no judgment has been issued.

Questions about Gordillo’s working-class credentials were also central to Monday’s exchange between Mamdani and reporters about Gordillo. The International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers told the New York Post that its Joint Apprentice Training Committee terminated Gordillo’s electrician apprenticeship in March after a "prolonged absence from and failure to participate in required work and classes."

FRUSTRATED BLUE-COLLAR UNION BOSSES RIP SOCIALIST POLITICIANS, WARN OF LABOR EXODUS FROM DEM PARTY

The New York Post reported that Gordillo later sought and received approval for a $95,000 annual salary from NYC-DSA without disclosing the termination to members. The outlet also reported that the Bed-Stuy renovation used nonunion contractors and was hit with a city stop-work order over permit issues—prompting further criticism of a DSA leader who has cast himself as a union electrician and advocate for working people.

A source close to the union, according to the New York Post, said Gordillo "didn’t have a strong work record to begin with" and took the job "just for show," while hogging "a slot from someone who probably really needed the opportunity."

item.title: Sue Bird claims WNBA players wanted to 'shut up and dribble' despite leading 2020 political push
item.description: Sue Bird now claims WNBA players wanted to "shut up and dribble" in 2020, but her own words from that era openly contradict her revisionist stance.
item.content:encoded:
"We would have loved to shut up and dribble."

That's what Sue Bird said on a recent episode of her podcast.

Yes, Sue Bird. The same woman who was engaged to Megan Rapinoe for more than five years before they announced their split earlier this year now claims that she wanted to "shut up and dribble" instead of diving headfirst into progressive politics in 2020.

Bird said the players "would have loved to shut up and dribble because that meant we were talking about basketball." But the "intersectionality of it all," she argued, meant they "kind of had to speak on these things."

My goodness. I'm not sure a more ridiculous piece of revisionist history has ever been uttered into a microphone.

WNBA SUDDENLY WANTS TO STICK TO BASKETBALL AFTER YEARS OF MAKING POLITICS PART OF THE PRODUCT

Bird was a WNBPA vice president in 2020. That was the season that the WNBA put Black Lives Matter on its courts, launched the Justice Movement and created a Social Justice Council.

The league and its players repeatedly spoke out on progressive political topics like voting rights, LGBTQ advocacy and gun control.

This wasn’t just a handful of players sounding off online, either. The league and union built it into the fabric of the season.

Players even went so far as to openly support a Democrat candidate for U.S. Senate by wearing shirts that said "Vote Warnock" prior to games.

Bird now wants people to believe they were forced to do all those things.

Here's the problem: Bird's new stance is openly contradicted by... Bird's old stance.

"Our season was going to have to be played with social justice messages, on our jerseys, on the floor, forefront."

That’s what Sue Bird said in an October 2020 interview with NPR.

Quite a bit different than "we would have loved to shut up and dribble," huh?

Bird didn’t just say she wanted social justice at the forefront of the WNBA’s 2020 season. She called it nonnegotiable for the players.

And Bird said the league was on board "right from the jump."

THE LEFT WANTS CAITLIN CLARK, SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM TO SHUT UP AND DRIBBLE WHEN IT COMES TO TRANS SPORTS

Then the WNBA got even more explicit. Players wore "Vote Warnock" shirts in support of Democrat Raphael Warnock during his Senate race against then-Atlanta Dream co-owner Kelly Loeffler.

Loeffler had criticized the WNBA for dedicating its season to Black Lives Matter, and the players’ union had already called for her ouster. Bird had a different idea: go after her Senate seat.

Axios reported the idea to publicly support Warnock came directly from Bird. "What a great way for us to get the word out about this man, and hopefully put him in the Senate," Bird said at the time.

In 2020, Bird was openly thinking about how WNBA players could help put a Democrat in the U.S. Senate.

In 2026, though, Bird says the WNBA has become a "lightning rod" for political fights the league office cannot be expected to solve. She brought up Donald Trump and wondered whether anyone, including Democrats, had figured out how not to be manipulated by the way he operates.

How, Bird asked, was the WNBA supposed to figure that out "overnight"? She said the league office might be getting too much flak for failing to handle things that even politicians paid to handle them cannot figure out.

STEPHEN A. SMITH BLAMES ‘THE RIGHT’ FOR WNBA FIRESTORM, SAYS LEAGUE ‘LEFT THE DOOR OPEN’

The through-line for all of Bird's commentary was remarkably consistent, although misguided. Her central claim was that the WNBA and its players were innocent victims and unwilling players in a political game in 2020 and they are, once again, going through the same problem.

But Bird’s guest on that episode, ESPN reporter Ramona Shelburne, correctly noted that's not exactly true. Shelburne called the WNBA "a more willing participant" in political conversations because its players are willing to weigh in on hot-button issues.

She said the WNBA sits in the middle of the culture wars, but players, coaches, front offices and the league all have a choice about whether to engage.

"Right now the choice seems to have been that you are engaging," Shelburne said.

Exactly.

In 2020, Bird called social-justice messaging nonnegotiable. And when players fought with Kelly Loeffler, she helped turn it into a campaign for Raphael Warnock.

Bird clearly knows the difference.

She's choosing revisionist history anyway.

item.title: Why August is the most dangerous month to ignore your data
item.description: Medicare Open Enrollment scams start with data broker targeting months before October. Learn why August is the time to remove your personal info.
item.content:encoded:
Medicare Open Enrollment doesn't start until Oct. 15. So why am I telling you to worry about this in August? Because by the time Oct. 15 arrives, scammers aren't starting their work. They're finishing it.

The scam calls you may hear this fall, including fake Medicare card offers and urgent Social Security warnings, are only the final step. Scammers often build their target lists long before they make contact. Here is how that targeting process works and what you can do now to make yourself and your family harder to scam.

THIS SATURDAY! Free live CyberGuy class: Protect Your Money From Today’s Biggest Threats

Join us Saturday, Aug. 29, at 10 a.m. ET for a free CyberGuy LIVE class covering five simple steps to help defend yourself against AI scams, fraud, identity theft and financial hacks. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will explain how to set up bank alerts, strengthen your account logins, protect your phone number, freeze your credit and help secure your retirement savings against unauthorized transfers. No technical experience is needed. You’ll also receive our financial protection checklist, and every registrant will get a link to the class recording afterward.

Reserve your free spot today at CyberGuyLive.com.

DR OZ WARNS MEDICARE SCAMMERS ARE STEALING BILLIONS — AND YOUR PERSONAL INFORMATION COULD BE NEXT

Two major dates put Medicare and Social Security on the minds of millions of Americans each fall.

Medicare Open Enrollment begins on Oct. 15 and runs through Dec. 7. During that period, people can review their coverage and make certain changes that generally take effect Jan. 1. That also means beneficiaries expect to receive plan information, advertisements and calls about their coverage.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics currently plans to release September 2026 inflation data on Oct. 14. That release will complete the third-quarter CPI-W figures used to calculate the 2027 Social Security COLA. The Social Security Administration says the next COLA will be announced in October 2026. Based on the current schedule, the announcement is expected on Oct. 14. The Senior Citizens League currently projects a 3.8% increase for 2027. That estimate has been generating headlines, but it isn't the official number. The final percentage will depend on inflation data for July, August and September. Scammers do not have to guess when people will be thinking about benefits. These dates are public and repeat every year.

Here's what almost nobody thinks about. A scam call often comes near the end of the process, not the beginning. Before a fraudster dials, someone has to decide whom to target. Consumer lists can help make that decision. The Justice Department has already shown in court how marketing data can end up in the hands of scammers.

Epsilon Data Management maintained a database covering roughly 100 million American households. Two former employees, Robert Reger and David Lytle, spent about a decade selling targeted consumer lists to people running fraud schemes. Epsilon used consumer data and algorithms to identify people who were likely to respond to certain offers. One fraudster bought nearly 100 lists and used them to defraud more than 218,000 victims of over $23.7 million. Epsilon paid $150 million to resolve the case. That included $22.5 million in criminal penalties and $127.5 million for victim compensation. In September 2024, a federal court sentenced Reger to 120 months in prison and Lytle to 48 months.

Epsilon was not alone. KBM Group employees sold consumer data to clients involved in fraudulent mass-mailing schemes. The company entered into an agreement requiring it to pay $33.5 million for victim compensation and an $8.5 million criminal fine. Macromark pleaded guilty to knowingly supplying lists of potential victims to fraudulent mass mailers. Many of the victims were older and vulnerable. The company agreed to pay $1 million in fines and forfeiture. These companies did not operate from hidden corners of the dark web. They were established marketing businesses with employees, clients and offices.

Legitimate marketing companies still sell consumer lists online. Vendors advertise databases of Americans age 65 and older, along with lists created specifically for businesses that want to contact people approaching their 65th birthday. Buyers can often filter those lists by age, location, income, homeownership and other demographic details. Some products also include names, mailing addresses, phone numbers, email addresses and estimated home values. Selling a marketing list does not automatically make the vendor or buyer a scammer. However, the market shows how easily someone can identify and contact a narrow group of older Americans. That is why August and September matter. The personal data already exists, the enrollment dates are public and anyone planning a fall fraud campaign can begin researching potential targets before the calls start.

WHAT A SCAMMER SEES THE MOMENT THEY GOOGLE YOUR NAME

A purchased list gets a scammer a name, an age and an address. That alone makes for a generic call. What turns a generic call into a convincing one is everything else that's sitting on people-search sites like Spokeo, Whitepages, BeenVerified and Intelius. As I've written before, those profiles routinely include address history, relatives' names and financial signals like property ownership and estimated home value. That's the difference between "Hello, I'm calling about your Medicare benefits" and "Hi Mr. Patterson, I'm calling about the plan at your address on Maple Street. Is your wife Linda still on the same coverage?" One of those calls gets hung up on. The other one gets answered.

You can run a quick free scan of how exposed you are online to get a better understanding of your data exposure. If it shows details you never consented to publishing, you'll be able to take action and get them removed. Get a free scan to find out if your personal information is already out on the web: CyberGuy.com.

A data removal service research team analyzed FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center data and found that 72% of the crimes reported by Americans over 60 in 2024 were facilitated or made worse by victims' personal data being available online. That's roughly 82,000 complaints out of 113,906. Those data-facilitated crimes accounted for $4.2 billion of the $4.9 billion older Americans reported losing that year. The average victim lost about $33,200. And this problem is growing, not shrinking. Reported elder fraud victims rose 45% in a single year. What the fall adds isn't a new kind of crime. It's a schedule.

The Federal Trade Commission puts it plainly: "Every year, scammers get more active around Medicare Open Enrollment Period, trying to get your money, information or both." The agency warns that callers pose as Medicare representatives, pressure people about a "new" or "updated" Medicare card, and spoof caller ID so the call appears to come from an official number.

Meanwhile, the Social Security version writes itself. Every October, a wave of "Claim Your COLA" scams tells retirees they have to take action to receive their increase or they'll lose it. They don't. The adjustment is automatic. But by October, that call arrives sounding perfectly timed, because it is.

That's the natural reaction. October feels like the real deadline. Why act now? Because the targeting gets locked in before the calls do. If your name, age, address, relatives and financial profile are sitting on broker sites this month, they're available to be compiled, sorted and resold well before anyone picks up a phone in October.

And removal isn't instant. Brokers have to process opt-out requests, and they re-list information on a rolling basis, which means the process works best when you start it early and let it run. Beginning in August means you're being scrubbed from the pipeline while it's still being assembled. Beginning in November means you're filing paperwork while the calls are already coming in. The point isn't to react faster. It's to be a worse target before anyone goes looking.

These steps can help reduce the personal information scammers may use and prepare your family before fall fraud attempts begin.

Go to Spokeo, Whitepages, BeenVerified or a similar site and look up your own name. See exactly what a caller would see this month, before they do.

If you have older relatives, their profiles are the ones worth the most to a scammer. An August check-in beats an October warning.

WHY CAREFUL PEOPLE STILL END UP ON DATA BROKER SITES

Every major broker is required to honor removal requests. The catch: there are hundreds of them, each with its own process, and they re-list your information regularly. Starting now gives the process time to work before the fall surge.

Removing your information from data brokers one site at a time can take hours. A reputable automated data removal service can submit opt-out requests on your behalf and continue checking participating sites in case your information reappears.

Some services also accept custom removal requests for people-search sites and other websites that publish personal details. Before signing up, compare the number of brokers covered, how often the service checks for new listings, whether it handles custom requests and whether independent experts have reviewed its privacy and security practices.

A family plan may offer better value when you want to protect parents, children or other members of your household. No service can remove every piece of information from the internet, but ongoing removals can reduce the personal details scammers may use to create convincing calls, messages or emails.

Check out my top picks for data removal services and get a free scan to find out if your personal information is already out on the web by visiting CyberGuy.com.

Agree on a code word with elderly parents or relatives today, while there's no pressure. It's a much easier conversation in August than in the middle of a panicked phone call in November.

If your bank still verifies you with "mother's maiden name" or "city you were born in," that information is likely already on a broker profile. Switch to answers that aren't true and store them in a password manager.

Medicare Open Enrollment runs from Oct. 15 through Dec. 7, while the 2027 Social Security COLA is expected to be announced on Oct. 14. Those public dates give scammers predictable events to reference in calls, texts and letters. Justice Department cases involving Epsilon, KBM Group and Macromark show that consumer information has been sold to fraud operations and used to identify older or vulnerable targets. The FBI received 201,266 complaints from people 60 and older in 2025, with reported losses reaching $7.748 billion. Incogni separately estimated that exposed personal information may have facilitated or worsened 72% of the 2024 crime categories it analyzed. Removing information from people-search sites cannot prevent every scam. However, reducing exposed details can make it harder for a criminal to create a convincing personal story. Social Security COLA increases are automatic. Medicare cards are mailed automatically and are free. Anyone demanding information or payment to activate either one should be treated as a potential scammer. You still have time before this year's open enrollment period begins. Search your name today and see what a stranger can learn before ever picking up the phone.

item.title: Sophie Cunningham gets cheeky and celebrates Dolly Parton, Dolphins fans brace for Tua & Dunkin's disrespect!

item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday–Friday on OutKick.com.

Over the hump and safely into the second half of the week. We're 48 hours away from college football, boys and girls. Two sleeps. That's it.

Will it feel like a college football Saturday? A real one? Eh. Probably not. No GameDay. No Big Noon. No full slate.

But after the insufferable summer we've just endured, a little UNC-TCU in Dublin will be welcomed with open arms. Everyone is out to get Bill Belichick right now. Paul Finebaum has been slandering the GOAT for months over on ESPN. It's disgusting.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Please, Lord, let UNC win. I need it.

Let's roll.

Welcome to a Thursday Nightcaps — the one where the Dolly Parton tributes keep rolling in, both from you guys AND from Sophie Cunningham.

I've been scanning the other WNBA socials and didn't see anyone else pay their respects to Dolly. Stunning!

What else? I've got an embarrassing Wednesday afternoon crowd out west, a loaded inbox after yesterday's question (I knew it would be), Dolphins fans are currently arguing about the dumbest thing imaginable, and you'll never guess what's already back at my local Dunks.

Disgusting. You'll see.

Grab you a regular coffee because it's only August 27th and you have an ounce of self-respect, and settle in for a Thursday 'Cap!

Couple things ...

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM THROWS ON A BACKLESS TOP AND OVERTAKES CAITLIN CLARK, TRUMP WAVES THE FLAG & GRUDEN'S BACK!

We all caught up now? Good!

Now, let's get this class started with Sophie Cunningham respecting Dolly Parton with a social media post that included the caption:

"My weaknesses have always been food and men — in that order." Dolly Parton

Wild little ride there from Sophie. What a twist at the end, too! Didn't see it coming. Not sure what was going on there or who Sophie was mooning, but we're all here to have fun, right?

Lord knows I'd take that over the nonsense that happened in Chicago earlier this week.

OK, let's keep the line moving and check the mailbox before we run out of time. Yesterday, I asked everyone for their top five heartbreaking moments as a sports fan.

As expected, you all brought it.

From Kevin W:

1.  Red sox come back from 3.

2. Wide right

3. Music city miracle…it was a forward pass

4. 13 seconds

5. It was a catch not an interception.

- I take it Kevin is a Bills and Yankees fan. Just a hunch.

From Matt C:

1. As a Devils fan, Matteau in 2OT in '94. It just cannot possibly get any worse than that in sports, although Bills fans could have an argument.

2. But as a Knicks fan, Charles Smith's missed layups against the Bulls in '93. That was our year.

3. As a Mets fan, Yadier Molina's homer in the top of the 9th, 2006 NLCS Game 7. It took me weeks to recover.

4. Back to the Knicks, Starks shooting 2-18 in the '94 Finals Game 7 against the Rockets. That was our year.

5. I'll just leave this slot reserved for Michael Jordan. It's an amalgamation of bad memories at this point. And in each of them, it was definitely our year. I still say the 90s Knicks have an argument as a legitimate dynasty, despite no ring.

- The 2006 NLCS was incredible. One of my favorite postseason baseball series ever.

From Brian S:

1. 1987 playoffs, finally ready to vanquish the Celtics. Isiah Thomas inbound pass stolen by Larry Bird, fed to Dennis Johnson, accompanied by that Johnny Most radio call.

2. 1987 was a great year! Syracuse missing countless FTs down the stretch, then having Keith Smart ripping the heart out of its first chance at a natty with the only shot he’ll ever be remembered for.

3. Carlos Beltran, bat on shoulder, watching Adam Wainwright’s curve end the 2006 NLCS.

4. Here’s a double-dipper San Francisco treat: Lions gagging on a 24-7 halftime lead to 49ers in 2025 NFC title game; Giants somehow blow a 38-14 third quarter lead to 49ers in the 2002 Wild Card.

5. And, most recently, the Mets trading Pete Crow Armstrong for Javy "Thumbs Down" Baez. That one might ascend higher as the years continue.

- I'm sensing a theme with New York sports fans today. You guys have had it ROUGH!

That picture of Trump watching Beltran strikeout to end the series resurfaces every few years, and it mesmerizes me every time. What a game. What a series.

Who knew we'd work in so much Mets-Cards '06 NLCS talk into today's class? It's why we win (hypothetical) awards!

OK, let's rapid-fire this Thursday class into a big night of FCS football. That's right.

FCS football:

Forget Saturday ... we get 22 (!!!) FCS football games tonight. Seems excessive, but I'll take anything after this summer.

Not sure why ESPN couldn't be bothered to put one on an actual network, but I reckon they have to sell those stupid ESPN+ subscriptions somehow.

Here's the real question, though: Do we think those 22 FCS games will have more butts in the seats than yesterday's Indians-Angels game did?

Lordy. What a scene! The official box score says they had over 25,000 fans in attendance. Do you buy that? Come on.

I don't blame Angels fans for one second, by the way. In a historically down year for the American League, they are still, somehow, the worst team in baseball. Do you understand how hard it is for an AL team to be out of the playoff race right now?

And yes, I know it was ... hot ... in Anaheim yesterday. The weather man tells me it was 92 degrees. The sun was out. A lot of the fans moved to shadier pastures in the stadium. I get it.

But still, it's such a bad look for a professional baseball team. Yikes.

On the way out, I'd like to leave everyone here with another question: Do players who left a team deserve to get booed upon their return?

Dolphins fans are planning to boo the heck out of Tua when he comes back tomorrow night as the preseason starter for the Falcons ...

And they absolutely, unequivocally should. I was a HUGE Tua guy for years. Massive. But then he signed a lucrative deal that he didn't deserve, became insufferably cocky and unlikeable, and started playing like dog-you-know-what before getting cut.

He also hamstrung the franchise with all of his dead money, although that goes on the GM as much as it does Tua.

But the broader point? Yes, former players who left on bad terms should get booed when they return. Could you imagine Philly fans having this debate?

Those sickos boo their teams three minutes into a new season! I've seen it. And I love it.

Anyway, let me know!

See you tomorrow.

Booing Tua OK? Email me at Zach.Dean@OutKick.com.

item.title: From Netflix to GPS: 10 ways this hidden tech infrastructure quietly powers modern life
item.description: Data centers power everything from streaming and gaming to AI chatbots and fraud detection. Here's how they quietly run the apps you use daily.
item.content:encoded:
Data centers are the hidden infrastructure behind much of modern life, powering everything from the apps on your phone and the shows you stream to online shopping, banking and artificial intelligence.

Inside these warehouse-sized facilities, thousands of servers store data, process digital requests and keep online services running around the clock. Most Americans may never see one, but they use them constantly—often without realizing it.

A SOUTHERN STATE JUST TOOK THE TOP SPOT IN ONE OF THE WORLD’S FASTEST-GROWING INDUSTRIES

"Anytime you’re touching technology and using everything from social media to your email, all of that information, all of the data is being processed in a data center," Brittany Kaiser, CEO of Alpha Compute, told Fox News Digital.

The recent race to build more facilities is being driven in large part by AI, which Kaiser said processes "way more data" than routine activities such as email and social media. But data centers are necessary for so much more than creating a speedy reply to your ChatGPT questions.

Here are 10 ways data centers quietly power the services Americans rely on every day.

From Instagram and TikTok to Gmail and banking apps, data centers process and store the information behind the services people use every day. When you open an app, upload a photo, refresh your feed or send a message, your phone is connecting to servers that retrieve and deliver that information in seconds.

The apps may live on a screen in your hand, but much of the work happens far away inside a physical facility filled with computers running continuously.

Netflix, YouTube, Spotify and other streaming platforms rely on massive computing infrastructure to deliver movies, videos and music to millions of users at once. Data centers help store enormous libraries of content and move it quickly enough to prevent the pauses and buffering that frustrate viewers.

Online games also rely on data centers to connect players, synchronize what is happening in a match and reduce the lag that can make a game unplayable. The more people stream, game and use data-heavy services, the more computing power those platforms need behind the scenes.

Every time someone asks an AI chatbot a question, generates an image or uses an AI-powered search feature, data centers provide the computing power working behind the screen. Those requests require far more processing than a basic web search because the systems must analyze information and generate a response in real time.

ONE OF AMERICA'S OLDEST MANUFACTURERS SAYS AI IS CREATING JOBS — NOT REPLACING THEM

That is a major reason the technology industry is racing to build bigger and more powerful data centers, often equipped with specialized chips designed for AI workloads.

Your iPhone photos, Google Drive documents and cloud backups do not just float around in cyberspace. They are stored on physical servers inside data centers, often with copies kept in multiple locations to help prevent data loss.

That means a lost phone or broken laptop does not necessarily mean lost memories or work files—but it also means the cloud depends on vast amounts of real-world hardware.

Search engines rely on data centers to sort through enormous amounts of information and return results in fractions of a second. Every query triggers systems that locate relevant webpages, images, maps, videos and other information before sending the results back to your device.

What feels like a simple Google search is actually a complex exchange between your device and powerful servers processing requests at enormous scale.

When you order something online, data centers help manage inventory, process payments, make product recommendations and track packages to your door. They also allow retailers to update product availability and pricing quickly as demand changes.

During major shopping events such as Black Friday, those systems have to handle a surge of shoppers and transactions without crashing.

Google Maps, Waze and other navigation services depend on computing infrastructure to process traffic patterns, routes and location data in real time. They combine information from roads, users, businesses and mapping systems to estimate travel times and suggest alternate routes.

Without the data centers behind them, navigation apps would not be able to react as quickly to accidents, congestion or changing road conditions.

Video calls, cloud-based software, shared documents and workplace messaging all rely heavily on data-center infrastructure. Every Zoom meeting, Slack message and live edit to a shared file depends on servers that keep information synced between people working from different locations.

For many companies, data centers have become as essential to day-to-day operations as office space, phones and electricity.

Banks, credit-card companies and retailers use powerful computing systems to flag suspicious transactions, verify purchases and help protect customers from fraud. Those systems can compare a purchase against patterns such as location, spending history and past transactions in a matter of seconds.

KEVIN O'LEARY WARNS CHINA IS WINNING THE AI RACE BECAUSE U.S. STATES ARE SLOWING DATA CENTER PRODUCTION

And that speed matters because a delayed fraud alert can give someone using a stolen card time to rack up multiple charges before the customer or bank can stop it.

Autonomous vehicles, advanced robotics, scientific research and other emerging technologies require increasingly powerful computing infrastructure. Data centers help train the AI systems behind those tools, process huge volumes of data and support the software that allows them to improve over time.

As more parts of the economy become digital, the data center is becoming less of a niche tech facility and more of the infrastructure supporting modern American life.

item.title: 2 airport workers are dead after malaria cases shock officials at major travel hub
item.description: Two employees at Frankfurt Airport in Germany died after six workers contracted airport malaria, prompting mosquito traps and genetic analysis of captured insects.
item.content:encoded:
Two employees have died after a cluster of malaria cases emerged among workers at Frankfurt Airport, and officials are investigating mosquitoes at the major German travel hub.

Six employees contracted a form of the disease known as "airport malaria" through their work at the airport, Fraport, the company that operates Frankfurt Airport, told Fox News Digital in a statement.

Based on a recent update from the Frankfurt Health Department, two of those employees died as a result of the infections, Fraport said.

POPULAR NYC MUSEUM TESTS POSITIVE FOR LEGIONNAIRES' DISEASE BACTERIA AMID OUTBREAK

"We are shocked and deeply saddened by the loss of our colleagues, and our thoughts are with their families and friends," the company said.

The other four affected workers have recovered, according to Fraport, which said its departments are closely monitoring the situation.

Malaria is a serious disease caused by a parasite and is most commonly spread to people through the bite of an infected mosquito, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

Early symptoms can include fever, chills, headache, muscle aches and fatigue, the CDC said. 

The disease can become severe or deadly if it is not diagnosed and treated quickly.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"We have provided comprehensive information to all employees and encourage them to consult a doctor if they experience any symptoms," Fraport said.

Employees were also advised to tell their doctors that they work at the airport and that cases of airport malaria have been reported there to help ensure appropriate medical examination and treatment, the company said.

Mosquito traps have also been installed at the airport, according to the company.

Mosquitoes caught in the traps will undergo genetic analysis by the Institute of Tropical Medicine in Antwerp, Belgium, to determine their species and origin, Fraport said.

Fox News Digital previously reported on heightened health measures at airports in parts of Asia earlier this year after an outbreak of the deadly Nipah virus in India.

The virus can spread between animals and people and can cause symptoms ranging from fever to brain infection and death, according to the Cleveland Clinic.

Following the outbreak, Thailand introduced monitoring and screening measures at international travel checkpoints, according to the country's Department of Disease Control.

Travelers showing a high fever or symptoms associated with Nipah could face additional screening and be asked to provide their travel history, possible exposure and when their symptoms began, the department said.

Health officials also issued precautions aimed at reducing the risk of infection, including guidance about food, water and contact with sick or dead animals.

item.title: Riley Gaines endorses Ken Paxton for Senate, cites fight to protect women's sports
item.description: Riley Gaines endorsed Ken Paxton in the Texas Senate race, citing his NCAA lawsuit and contrasting his record with James Talarico on transgender athletes.
item.content:encoded:
Women’s sports advocate Riley Gaines endorsed Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton in his U.S. Senate race against Democratic state Rep. James Talarico, pointing to the candidates’ sharply different records on transgender athletes and medical treatments for minors.

"Texas needs a senator who will fight without apology for women, for kids, and for the health of every American family," Gaines said in a statement. "Ken Paxton is that leader, and I am proud to support and endorse him."

Gaines, a former University of Kentucky swimmer, became a prominent advocate for preserving female-only athletic divisions after tying transgender swimmer Lia Thomas in the 200-yard freestyle at the 2022 NCAA championships.

TEXAS AG KEN PAXTON SENDS MESSAGE TO WNBA AMID 'CONCERNS' OVER TREATMENT OF SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SUPPORTERS

She praised Paxton as a "relentless fighter for the protection of children" and highlighted his legal action against the NCAA.

"He has taken decisive action against those who would expose our children to irreversible harm and refused to be silent while the radical left was putting the next generation in danger," Gaines said. "He even filed a major lawsuit against the NCAA to keep men out of women’s sports."

Paxton sued the NCAA in December 2024, accusing the organization of violating the Texas Deceptive Trade Practices Act by marketing competitions as women’s events while allowing transgender athletes to participate. The lawsuit sought to prevent transgender athletes from competing in NCAA women’s events involving Texas teams or taking place in the state. The NCAA later changed its policy in February 2025 to restrict women’s competition to athletes who were female at birth.

Paxton has also filed lawsuits against doctors he accused of violating a Texas law prohibiting certain transition-related treatments for minors.

TALARICO'S MOVE TO SWAP OUT 'WOMAN' RESURFACES AMID BACKLASH OVER SIMILAR BILL IN NY: 'INSANE INDIVIDUAL'

Gaines contrasted Paxton’s record with that of Talarico, who opposed legislation requiring Texas public-school athletes to compete on teams corresponding with their biological sex.

"His opponent, James Talarico, is a far-left extremist who has refused to accept biological reality," Gaines said. "He has repeatedly put women’s safety, privacy, and opportunities in danger by championing a radical agenda that forces biological males into girls’ and women’s sports, locker rooms, and private spaces."

During debate over a school sports bill in 2021, Talarico argued that biological sex could be "a spectrum" and invoked his Christian faith while defending transgender children. He later said he still believes transgender people deserve "dignity and equality," although he would express some of his earlier comments differently today. The Texas Tribune reported that Talarico opposed the legislation that ultimately became Texas’ school sports law.

Talarico has separately said he opposes gender-reassignment surgery for minors. His campaign has argued that Republican attacks distort his position and ignore his objections to the broader scope of Texas’ treatment restrictions. PolitiFact reported in June that advertisements depicting Talarico as supporting such surgeries were inaccurate.

Paxton defeated longtime Sen. John Cornyn in the Republican runoff in May. Talarico defeated Rep. Jasmine Crockett in the Democratic primary. The two will face each other in the Nov. 3 general election, which has emerged as one of the country’s most competitive Senate contests.

item.title: Trump keeps winning Republican primaries; his losses may be more revealing

In gubernatorial showdowns, Trump-backed candidates have suffered a handful of high-profile defeats, but overall, 16 of the 21 contenders for governor the president has endorsed have captured the party's nomination.

This week, Trump-backed candidates scored statewide victories in two very competitive contests.

Trump-endorsed Sen. Darline Graham of South Carolina, who was recently appointed to fill the remaining months of her late brother Sen. Lindsey Graham's current term, edged conservative Rep. Ralph Norman in a runoff to win the GOP Senate nomination for November's election. WHAT THE LATEST FOX NEWS POWER RANKINGS IN THE MIDTERM RACES SHOW

Trump backed Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette for the GOP gubernatorial nomination — in the race to succeed the term-limited McMaster — ahead of the state's early June primary.

Evette was the top vote-getter in the primary but lost the ensuing runoff election against South Carolina Attorney General Alan Wilson in a landslide. And Trump, ever hungry for a victory, endorsed Wilson in addition to Evette days before the runoff.

It's undeniable that Trump has dramatically reshaped the GOP since his first White House victory a decade ago, with the populist MAGA and America First wings gaining prominence over more traditional fiscal and social conservatives.

"The Republican Party is Trump’s party, and there’s no question that an endorsement from the president provides a tremendous boost in a Republican primary. But it doesn’t necessarily mean the candidate’s going to win," veteran GOP strategist and communicator Ryan Williams told Fox News Digital.

Williams said that "the president still has a firm grip on the party, even in places where a candidate he backed loses a nomination." But he noted that "if there are underlying issues with a candidacy, those can pose problems that even an endorsement can’t overcome."

item.title: Trump floats renaming the Atlantic and Pacific oceans after rebranding historic lake
item.description: President Donald Trump joked the Atlantic and Pacific oceans could be next after signing the executive order renaming Lake Ontario to Lake America immediately.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump on Thursday signed an executive order renaming Lake Ontario "Lake America," then joked that the Atlantic and Pacific oceans could be next.

"As you know, we took something called the Gulf of Mexico, we changed it, and now it's very routinely the Gulf of America," Trump said.

"So if you think about it, we have a gulf and we have a lake. Now all we need is an ocean," he continued. "So maybe we'll have to change the name of the Atlantic and or the Pacific. Maybe we'll change them both."

VANCE SAYS CANADA FRIENDLIER TO CHINA ON TRADE THAN TO US: 'INSANITY'

Trump declared the Lake Ontario change "official, effective immediately" while announcing the order.

"And finally, it's the purpose of this more than anything else is we're going to be changing the name of Lake Ontario, effective immediately to Lake America," Trump said. "That's going to take place right now as I signed the order."

‘CAPTAIN CANADA’ FIREBRAND UNLOADS ON TRUMP WITH PROFANE ONE-LINER AS TRADE WAR ESCALATES

The president said the administration had "filed all the necessary papers, documents, everything else" and notified the relevant parties.

"So we've done everything that you have to do. And this is official, effective immediately," Trump said.

CANADA REPORTEDLY SCRAPS JOINT BRIDGE CELEBRATION WITH US AFTER TRUMP RENEWS TARIFF THREAT

The order directs Interior Secretary Doug Burgum, working with the Board on Geographic Names, to take steps within 30 days to rename the lake in the federal Geographic Names Information System and remove references to "Lake Ontario." 

It also directs the board to ensure federal maps, contracts, documents and agency communications use the new name.

TRUMP BLAMES CANADA FOR WILDFIRE SMOKE, SAYS POLLUTION COSTS SHOULD BE ADDED TO TARIFFS

The order does not control the name used by Canada, which borders the lake along with New York.

It is not Trump’s first effort to put an American stamp on a major body of water.

On his first day back in office, Trump signed Executive Order 14172, "Restoring Names That Honor American Greatness," directing the federal government to use "Gulf of America" in place of the Gulf of Mexico.

TRUMP JUST EXPANDED HIS TARIFF PLAYBOOK WITH A POWERFUL TRADE WEAPON NO PRESIDENT HAS EVER USED

Trump later signed a proclamation declaring Feb. 9, 2025, the first "Gulf of America Day" while aboard Air Force One over the newly renamed gulf en route to Super Bowl LIX in New Orleans.

"Today, I am very honored to recognize February 9, 2025, as the first ever Gulf of America Day," Trump wrote in the proclamation.

CHAD WOLF: CANADA CAN'T EXPECT FREE TRADE WHILE LEAVING OUR NORTHERN BORDER VULNERABLE

Burgum said at the time that the Interior Department had implemented Trump’s instruction from the executive order.

The Lake America order invokes that same policy, arguing that the United States is the "greatest protector" of the Great Lakes system. 

It points to nearly $4 billion in U.S. freshwater ecosystem investment over the last decade, as well as the Coast Guard’s fleet of icebreaking vessels.

SENATORS REJECT TRUMP’S CALL TO MAKE CANADA PAY FOR WILDFIRE SMOKE: ‘RIDICULOUS’

"The United States has invested nearly $4 billion in protecting the Great Lakes freshwater ecosystem in the last decade, while Canada has invested far less in similar initiatives over the same period," the order states.

The order also cites the lake’s historic role in American trade, settlement, defense, commerce and energy, arguing it remains a major economic and strategic resource for the United States.

"In recognition of this flourishing economic resource and its critical importance to our Nation’s economy and its people, I am directing that the Lake officially be renamed as Lake America," Trump wrote.

Trump’s comments about renaming the Atlantic and Pacific appeared to be a joke. He announced no executive action or formal effort targeting either ocean.

The White House did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

item.title: Out-of-this-world fix for data center backlash could be on NASA's horizon
item.description: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman says solar-powered AI data centers in Earth's orbit could solve America's fights over land, water and grid capacity.
item.content:encoded:
NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman is backing a once-futuristic answer to America’s fight over AI data centers: Move them into Earth's orbit.

Isaacman said Wednesday that solar-powered facilities in space could tap the sun’s energy without competing for the land, water and grid capacity required by sprawling data centers proposed across the country.

"Let’s take our data centers, put them in Earth orbit, take advantage of that free fusion reactor that’s out there for us and use that to ensure we do win the space race for sure, but the AI race, too," Isaacman said in an interview with Nexstar DC.

Isaacman’s idea comes as voters push back on the data center boom. A Fox News poll this summer found 70% of voters oppose building AI data centers in their own area, while 79% said construction should slow to address environmental and community concerns rather than move as quickly as possible to maintain a competitive edge over China.

TRUMP TO HONOR ARTEMIS II ASTRONAUTS WHO TRAVELED FARTHER FROM EARTH THAN ANY HUMANS IN HISTORY

Half of those opposed said environmental issues, including energy and water use, pollution and noise, were their chief concern.

The idea comes with its own engineering problems. AI chips produce immense heat, and satellites would have to release it through large radiators. Operators would also need cheap, reliable launches, radiation-resistant hardware and laser links fast enough to connect thousands of computers spread across orbit.

That has not stopped companies from trying to turn the concept into a business. Google has called Project Suncatcher a "moonshot" to place its TPU chips on solar-powered satellites linked by lasers. It plans to launch two prototype satellites by early 2027 to test its hardware in orbit and determine whether the satellites can share data fast enough for AI workloads.

PETER NAVARRO: TRUMP'S ARTEMIS VISION IS NOW FLYING — AND CHINA IS PAYING ATTENTION

SpaceX is pursuing a more aggressive version. Its proposed AI1 satellite would stand about 98 feet tall, have a wingspan of roughly 246 feet and carry up to 175 kilowatts of average AI computers, according to the company. SpaceX says it is building a Texas factory intended to produce thousands of the satellites as early as late 2027.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Small-scale tests are already underway. Startup Starcloud launched a satellite carrying a Nvidia H100 chip in November and says it later ran a version of Google’s Gemini model and trained a small language model in space. Starcloud plans its first commercial mission, Starcloud-2, for 2027.

SpaceX has also asked the Federal Communications Commission for authority to deploy as many as 1 million orbital data-center satellites between 500 and 2,000 kilometers above Earth. The satellites would use optical links to communicate with one another and SpaceX’s Starlink network. The FCC has accepted the application for review but has not approved the constellation.

item.title: PXG throws jab at Good Good and Callaway Golf with driver ad of its own amid controversy
item.description: PXG's new ad featuring LPGA Tour players and the caption "our drivers play nice with everyone" appears to target the Good Good and Callaway controversy.
item.content:encoded:
One major golf brand has jumped right into the controversy and drama created by another, as the advertising world in the golf space has never been under a bigger microscope.

Parsons Xtreme Golf, more widely known as PXG, is still very much a young brand in the grand scheme of things, having only been established in 2014, but that didn't stop it from diving into the mess brought forth by Good Good and Callaway.

PXG shared an ad on its social channels featuring a number of its different LPGA Tour players hitting and promoting the brand's newest driver. The caption, "our drivers play nice with everyone," accompanied by the hashtag #SheGolfs," almost certainly had a very specific meaning behind it.

GOOD GOOD ISSUES CONTRADICTORY APOLOGY FOR SINCE-DELETED GOLF AD SHOWING A MAN SHOVING A WOMAN TO THE GROUND

PXG's video was shared a few days after the advertisement that Good Good and Callaway shared, quickly deleted, and has since apologized multiple times for, after it showed a man shoving a woman to the ground.

Good Good, the YouTube and apparel giant, and Callaway, one of the most well-known brands in golf, collaborated on a new driver. As part of its promotion for the new club, it teamed up for an advertisement, although the two wish they had gone in a different creative direction.

The video showed Good Good co-founder Garrett Clark shoving member Alexis Miestowski to the turf after she was seen reaching for a driver in a golf bag. Clark sprints at her, shoves her to the ground with his forearms, and stands over her before saying, "Do not touch my new driver."

While PXG's video does not directly mention either of the other two brands or the ad, the caption, coupled with it being shared just a few days after the Good Good and Callaway ad, makes it hard to believe it is a coincidence.

"We posted a video to our channels that ultimately depicted actions that are not aligned with our values as a brand,"Good Good's first statement about the ad explained. "We have since taken that content down. And sincerely apologize. Good Good has always stood for making the game of golf more inclusive to all, and we will continue to ensure that is our mission moving forward."

BACKLASH OVER GOOD GOOD GOLF AD GOES TOO FAR AS STORES PULL MERCHANDISE, PGA TOUR EVENT POTENTIALLY CANCELED

On August 25, Callaway issued a statement apologizing for the advertisement and admitting that it had approved the ad before it was shared online. Two days later, Callaway announced it was cutting ties with Good Good and donating $1 million to causes and programs that help prevent violence against women.

Following initial statements, Front Office Sports reported on Wednesday that Dick's Sporting Goods, Golf Galaxy, and the PGA Tour Superstore had pulled Good Good's merchandise from their shelves.

The PGA Tour is set to host the Good Good Championship at Omni Barton Creek Resort & Spa’s Fazio Canyons Course in Austin, Texas, in November 2026. It has been rumored that the Tour could be looking to cut ties with Good Good and seek a new sponsor for the event.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: House committee probes Chicago Public Schools over hiding 'gender affirmation' from parents
item.description: Chicago Public Schools CEO Macquline King faced House committee scrutiny over gender identity policies that allegedly hide students' transitions from parents.
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE — The House Committee on Education and the Workforce is demanding Chicago Public Schools (CPS) Superintendent and CEO Macquline King respond to concerns that schools are hiding information regarding students' gender transitions from parents.

In a letter obtained by Fox News Digital, Committee Chair Rep. Tim Walberg, R-Mich., reached out to King in response to her testimony at a June 10 hearing titled, "Breaking Trust: Attacks on Parental Rights, Inappropriate Content, and Legal Abuses in America’s Schools."

"When asked by Rep. Mary Miller, R-Ill., at the June 10 hearing about CPS’ 'socially transitioning children without parental knowledge or consent,' [King] responded, '[w]e do not hide information from parents.' However, several of CPS’s policies and resources suggest otherwise," Walberg wrote.

TRUMP ADMIN TARGETS WOKE SCHOOLS ACCUSED OF HIDING STUDENTS' GENDER TRANSITIONS FROM PARENTS

Walberg cited CPS' interim guidelines along with a "Gender Diversity Toolkit" that prohibit staff members from disclosing a student's "transgender status or gender-nonconforming presentation" without the student's permission and clarified that parental consent is not required.

The Michigan congressman expressed concerns that the vague language of the guidelines could prevent faculty from communicating with parents about students' gender identity, which could go against the Supreme Court's ruling in Mirabelli v. Bonta earlier this year.

"When Rep. Bob Onder, R-Mo., asked you at the June 10 hearing whether CPS had made any changes in its policies to align with the Supreme Court’s decision in Mirabelli, you deflected and failed to give a clear, direct answer. You stated that you 'hope[d]' that 'the parent, the families, the student … and the school would all be in communication,'" Walberg wrote.

TRUMP DOJ CORNERS SCHOOL DISTRICT WITH 7-DAY ULTIMATUM OVER TRANS POLICY KEEPING PARENTS IN THE DARK

"Notably, while you stated that CPS communicates with parents in compliance with Illinois state law, you failed to specify whether CPS complies with federal law or Mirabelli," he continued. "CPS’s policies appear to undermine the authority of parents and guardians, which the Supreme Court has stated 'have primary authority with respect to the upbringing and education of children.’"

The Supreme Court ruled in Mirabelli v. Bonta that parents were likely to succeed in their claims that a California law prohibiting schools from disclosing to parents their child’s "gender identity" violated their free exercise rights under the First Amendment and their substantive due process rights under the 14th Amendment, though the case still remains in litigation at the 9th Circuit Court of Appeals.

Meanwhile, Walberg and the committee are requesting all guidance documents, written complaints and professional development training related to gender and sexuality with a response no later than Sept. 11.

LOUDOUN COUNTY PARENTS NOT 'SATISFIED' AFTER SCHOOL OFFICIALS TESTIFY ON TRANSGENDER POLICIES

In a comment to Fox News Digital, Walberg added, "Parents deserve the right to know what goes on in their child’s classroom and have a say in decisions regarding their child. That is commonsense, and that right doesn’t go away at the schoolhouse door. 

"Yet, far too often we have seen policies that allow schools to withhold important information from parents and make decisions about a child’s name, pronouns or gender identity without their knowledge.

"Our committee will always stand up for parents’ rights and defend their God-given role in their children’s lives and education."

Fox News Digital reached out to Chicago Public Schools for comment but did not immediately receive a response.
